data.summary: Gate bug in the shared xtask: gate --branch can leave an old commit's xtask in the caller's target dir, and the next gate run is a silent pass
data.body: Found while porting xtask (our branch worktree-agent-a877a9cd7259eb95c). gate --branch builds each older commit in the caller's CARGO_TARGET_DIR. Afterwards, `cargo xtask` in the same worktree ran the first commit's empty xtask stub: exit 0, no output, so a second gate run looked like a pass. Your gate handles the target dir the same way, as far as we can see. Suggested fix: build each commit under its own target dir (or one keyed by commit), and have gate refuse a binary built from a commit that isn't HEAD. We haven't changed it here, since VectorCraft holds the master copy; our workaround is running gate from a separate xtask build.

data.summary: VC verify has two fail-open paths our review found: dofile matched as literal text, and an unreadable oracle/ read as no fixtures
data.body: Codex found both in our port of your xtask verify. Our fix is b698dcb (branch worktree-agent-a877a9cd7259eb95c, under review), and we read your main efa66b4 for the same code. 1. map_deps (xtask/src/verify.rs ~3197) looks for the literal `dofile(`, so `dofile ("x.lua")`, a comment before the parenthesis, or a call with no parentheses loads a map whose hash the manifest needn't list; loadfile and require aren't seen at all. Ours now reads the map as Lua tokens and refuses loadfile, require, load, loadstring, any other use of the name dofile, and computed paths. 2. The stray-trace scan in check_games (~3698) is `if let Ok(fs::read_dir(..))` plus `.flatten()`: an unreadable oracle/ skips the scan and per-entry errors are dropped. load_fixture_manifests (~3560) also drops entry errors, and research.rs check (~127) and check_game (~150) treat an unreadable oracle/ as no fixtures. Ours lets only NotFound mean no fixtures. Regressions in b698dcb: every_spelling_of_dofile_is_followed, loading_forms_verify_cant_follow_are_refused, an_unreadable_oracle_directory_fails. Take them once it lands, or ask for the diff.

Both pieces are ported on branch `port-gate-host`: the build host and the scratch-worktree sweep. The tip, 81f8d03, passes `cargo xtask gate --branch` and its branch review approves it. The first review (of db45a34) found one high-severity problem; it is fixed in the last commit. Nothing is landed or pushed, and main is still 666b30f, so no rebase was needed.

Worktree: `/Users/jamess/GitHub/avoidmissingball/.claude/worktrees/agent-port-gate-host`.

## Commits (666b30f..81f8d03)
1. **8c331c4** Stamp version 3: adds the gating xtask's source hash, the `host` name and the `xtask-commit` lines. Versions 1 and 2 still read. A stamp that names a host is trusted only if its xtask was built from the tip and its source hash matches the tip's files as git holds them. It reuses the existing `srchash.rs` rather than adding a second copy.
2. **31c6242** The build host: `xtask/src/gate_host.rs`, `tools/gate-host`, and `--host` on `gate --branch` and `land`.
   - **Off by default:** a host runs only when `~/.config/avoidmissingball/gate-host` names it. With no file, or a different host, it errors and runs nothing; no flag or `local` gates on this Mac. No agent writes that file, and the call is recorded in `docs/decisions.md`.
   - **Tests:** they use a fake ssh and cargo; nothing contacts a real host. The "Connection to bytecut closed" and "blackhole" lines in the test output are printed by that fake ssh.
3. **61400d6** The sweep: `xtask/src/gate_scratch.rs`, mounted as `gate::scratch`, plus `gate --sweep [--dry-run]`.
   - **Locking:** each scratch tree is created locked with its gate's pid and start time, and a watchdog removes it when the gate dies.
   - **Sweeping:** each new scratch sweeps trees whose gate is dead.
   - **Removal fallback:** it now deletes only the tree's own git entry, where it used to run a repo-wide prune.
   - **Kept:** our mkdir-plus-counter naming (`claim_dir`).
4. **db45a34** Docs:
   - `docs/sync.md`: the VectorCraft commits taken (main 571fc244: `gate_host.rs` and `tools/gate-host` at 9a4573a4, `gate_scratch.rs` at 398575d5, gate.rs at 8625a18a).
   - `docs/decisions.md`: four delegated calls, with the two earlier "left out" rows marked as replaced.
   - `docs/tech-reference.md`: the lookup findings.
   - The new prose went through `/avoid-ai-writing`. That pass was model-only: its detector and checker scripts did not run.
5. **81f8d03** Review fix. `tools/gate-host` ran `git worktree prune` across the whole host repository after every run. That could drop another worktree's entry and leave a commit only it held open to garbage collection. It now removes only its own run's entry. The new test failed on db45a34 with "the other tree's entry was pruned".

## Failure cases covered by tests
Every new test fails on 666b30f; the commit messages say how.
- **Gates that die:** killed by KILL, TERM, INT or HUP, including when the parent had those signals ignored. A child process still working in the tree keeps it until that child exits.
- **Zombies and pid reuse:** `ps` tells a gone, zombie or running owner apart, and a reused pid is caught by the start time, read the same under any time zone.
- **Refusals:**
  - a live process in the tree, or `lsof` failing;
  - a branch checked out;
  - changed, untracked or ignored files, each named in the reason;
  - a lock that changed while the sweep ran;
  - `ps` failing.
- **Unsaved commits:** a dead tree's commit that only a side branch holds is archived under `refs/archive/amb-gate/` before removal, both by the sweep and by the watchdog.
- **Failed removals:** the fallback leaves other trees' entries alone, a deleted tree whose HEAD can't be read keeps its entry, and a failed `worktree add` cleans up its directory (or reports why it couldn't).
- **Races:** two scratches created in the same instant get different paths.
- **Host:** a lost connection reattaches, a host lost for good cleans itself up, a forged or mismatched host stamp is not trusted, and a host run leaves other worktrees alone.

## Left out
`--ci`, the bounded idle wait, `check_this_build` and `hold_target`: neither the host nor the sweep needs them. Because `check_this_build` is missing, a build with no valid source hash writes no `xtask` line in its stamp. The caffeinate wake lock was taken, since a sleeping Mac cut the host's ssh connections; it covers host gates only.

## To copy to the other projects
- **VectorCraft** should take four changes:
  - the host stays off until an owner config names it;
  - a dead tree's HEAD counts as saved only on main or an archive ref (VectorCraft accepts any ref, so a feature branch deleted after landing loses the commit);
  - a kept tree's reason names every path a removal would lose, not just the first;
  - the targeted cleanup in `tools/gate-host`, which has the same repo-wide prune.
  
  Smaller: `Stamp::by` skips an invalid hash.
- **BewareILive** has none of this: no host, stamp v3 or sweep.
